questions.prompt: Which statement best describes communication as a process?

options.text: A one-time act that ends when a sender speaks
A connected exchange in which people create, interpret, and respond to meaning
A rule that makes all receivers interpret a message identically
A record of words without attention to context or response

questions.explanation: Communication includes creation, conveyance, interpretation, and response. Sending alone does not show that meaning was shared.
questions.misconception: A delivered message is automatically a successful communication event.

questions.prompt: A student council writes and publishes a notice about a campus activity. In that event, the student council is the ____.

channel
noise
feedback

questions.explanation: The sender or source initiates a message for a purpose. The notice is the message, while the publication route is the channel.

questions.prompt: Turning a broad concern into three written action points for a team is an example of ____.

options.text: decoding
encoding
feedback
noise

questions.explanation: Encoding turns an idea or purpose into signs that can be conveyed. The action points are the chosen form of the idea.

questions.prompt: What does decoding involve?

options.text: Choosing the sender's purpose before any message exists
Selecting a platform without considering its users
Noticing and interpreting signs to assign meaning
Removing every possible difference between people

questions.explanation: Decoding is the receiver's interpretive work. It is shaped by attention, experience, language, and context, so it is not a perfect copy of intention.
questions.misconception: Receivers simply retrieve a fixed meaning that the sender placed inside the message.

questions.prompt: What is a useful strength of a linear communication model?

options.text: It helps inspect whether information moved from source to receiver
It proves that the receiver has the same meaning as the sender
It explains every cultural and relational influence
It shows that feedback is impossible in every situation

questions.explanation: A linear model is useful for a one-way alert or announcement when reach and delivery are the main questions. It is limited because it downplays feedback and context.

questions.prompt: A transactional view is most useful when you want to notice ____.

questions.explanation: Transactional models emphasize ongoing mutual influence and context. They do not claim that power or access is equal in every exchange.
